item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00300","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C24","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child's foreign-assistance administration order. Most notably, both authorize the officer administering a foreign-assistance statute to allocate program funds to other federal departments, agencies, or establishments. The child expands and adapts that same machinery by naming the Secretary of State, adding wholly-owned corporations, requiring obligation and expenditure under approved programs, and adding coordination with defense and economic-cooperation officials. C24 is also close in its delegation of presidential foreign-assistance functions to the Secretary of State, but that formula alone is less distinctive. C15 supplies relevant interagency foreign-aid consultation and transfer machinery, though its operative structure is less closely matched.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Funds appropriated or otherwise made available for the purposes of carrying out the portions of the Act ... may be allocated by the Secretary of State to any agency, department, establishment, or wholly-owned corporation of the Government for obligation and expenditure in accordance with programs approved by the Secretary of State","parent_excerpt":"The Administrator for Economic Cooperation is hereby authorized and directed to make appropriate allocations, for the purposes of Titles I and IV of the Act ... to any department, agency, or establishment of the Government, from such funds as shall be made available","explanation":"This is substantially the same statutory-program funding machinery, adapted from economic cooperation to mutual defense assistance and supplemented with program-approval controls."},{"child_excerpt":"The Secretary of State is authorized and directed to perform the functions and exercise the powers and authority vested in the President by the act","parent_excerpt":"The Administrator for Economic Cooperation is hereby authorized and directed to make appropriate allocations, for the purposes of Titles I and IV of the Act","explanation":"Both begin by assigning administration of specified portions of a new foreign-assistance statute to a principal officer and then define the officer's implementing authority."}]}
